genes/PSEPK/kdpA/kdpA-ai-review.yaml.description: KdpA (PP_4161) is the potassium-binding and potassium-translocating subunit of the KdpFABC high-affinity ATP-driven potassium uptake pump of the Pseudomonas putida inner membrane. By orthology with the structurally characterized Escherichia coli KdpA, it is a ten-helix member of the superfamily of potassium transporters whose KcsA-derived selectivity filter (TNGGG motif conserved in this protein) binds periplasmic K+ and forms the K+-selective pathway, while the P-type ATPase subunit KdpB supplies the energy for transport. The gene lies in a kdpABC operon with the KdpD/KdpE two-component regulatory system.

review.reason: KdpA is a ten-helix polytopic membrane protein; the E. coli ortholog is experimentally located in the inner membrane and the PSEPK sequence retains the predicted ten-helix topology.

genes/PSEPK/kdpB/kdpB-ai-review.yaml.description: KdpB (PP_4160, kdpFABC operon) is the catalytic P-type ATPase subunit (type IA, EC 7.2.2.6) of the KdpFABC high-affinity ATP-driven potassium uptake complex in the inner membrane of Pseudomonas putida KT2440. By orthology with the characterised Escherichia coli enzyme, it binds Mg-ATP in its cytoplasmic N and P domains, forms an aspartyl-phosphate intermediate on the conserved DKTGT aspartate (Asp311 here), and couples ATP hydrolysis to K+ uptake: K+ is selected by the channel-like KdpA subunit, transferred through an intramembrane tunnel to sites in the KdpB transmembrane domain, and released by KdpB to the cytoplasm.

Evidence from the E. coli ortholog (orthology-based support): Mg-ATP is the substrate and KdpC engages the KdpB nucleotide-binding loop.

genes/PSEPK/kdpC/kdpC-ai-review.yaml.description: KdpC (Q88FD8) is the small single-pass accessory subunit of the KdpFABC high-affinity ATP-driven potassium uptake pump of the Pseudomonas putida inner membrane. By orthology with the structurally characterized Escherichia coli complex, KdpC carries a periplasmic soluble domain that packs against the K+-selective subunit KdpA and, together with KdpF, stabilizes the KdpA-KdpB assembly; it neither hydrolyzes ATP (a KdpB function) nor forms the K+ pathway (a KdpA function). An earlier biochemical model in E. coli proposed that KdpC binds ATP and acts as a catalytic chaperone for KdpB, but the periplasmic location of its soluble domain in the structures makes that role uncertain.

review.reason: E. coli KdpC was reported to bind ATP (abstract-only evidence), but KdpFABC structures place the KdpC soluble domain in the periplasm, opposite the cytoplasmic nucleotide-binding domain of KdpB. KdpB is the ATP-binding subunit. The claim is contested in the ortholog and has no PSEPK-specific support; this matches the E. coli KdpC review.

genes/PSEPK/kdpD/kdpD-ai-review.yaml.description: KdpD (PP_4158; Q88FD9) is the predicted inner-membrane sensor histidine kinase of the KdpD/KdpE two-component system of Pseudomonas putida KT2440, encoded next to kdpE and the kdpFABC operon for the high-affinity K+ uptake pump. It has the full-length KdpD architecture: a cytoplasmic N-terminal KdpD domain and Usp domain, four transmembrane helices, and a cytoplasmic HisKA/HATPase_c transmitter. By orthology with E. coli KdpD it autophosphorylates and phosphorylates KdpE in response to K+ limitation, and likely also dephosphorylates KdpE~P.

genes/PSEPK/kdpE/kdpE-ai-review.yaml.description: KdpE (PP_4157; Q88FE0) is the predicted OmpR/PhoB-family response regulator of the KdpD/KdpE two-component system of Pseudomonas putida KT2440, encoded next to kdpD. It has an N-terminal receiver domain with the phosphorylatable Asp55 and a C-terminal OmpR/PhoB winged helix-turn-helix DNA-binding domain. By orthology with E. coli KdpE, phosphorylation by KdpD activates KdpE to bind the cis-regulatory sequence upstream of the kdpFABC promoter and activate transcription of the high-affinity K+ uptake pump KdpFABC.

genes/PSEPK/kdpF/kdpF-ai-review.yaml.description: KdpF is a 29-residue single-pass transmembrane peptide of Pseudomonas putida KT2440, encoded immediately upstream of kdpA in the kdpFABC operon, and a subunit of the KdpFABC high-affinity ATP-driven potassium uptake complex of the inner membrane.
